summary: Single Playwright spec covers all three mandated AC (URL, <html lang>, button text, EN Zod validation) with real string assertions sourced from en.json/uk.json. Test is ~22 LOC, linear, no mocks/fixtures/skip/retry, matches the task's 'keep it small' constraint. Litmus test passes on every assertion: removing a corresponding piece of locale wiring (LangSwitcher click handler, useLocaleHead lang, t() in submit button, Zod schema in computed) would break a specific assertion. The chosen hydration/wait pattern (waitForLoadState('networkidle') + expect.poll on URL) is defensible but introduces a couple of small CI-flake risks worth flagging non-blocking.

non_blocking_findings.issue: waitForLoadState('networkidle') is a known flaky knob in Nuxt dev mode — HMR websocket and Vite's lazy chunk-fetching can keep the network 'almost-idle' threshold dancing. In CI, where dev server is freshly spawned, idle is usually reachable; but if a future task adds polling (e.g. session probe, analytics beacon) the gate may never fire and the LangSwitcher click will race hydration. Playwright's official guidance is to wait for a concrete DOM/role signal instead.
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Replace `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` with a wait on the LangSwitcher being interactive, e.g. `await expect(page.locator('[data-test="lang-en"]')).toBeEnabled()` (or `.toBeVisible()` if the element renders disabled-then-enabled). This anchors on the exact precondition for the next click instead of a global network heuristic. Keeps LOC count the same.

non_blocking_findings.issue: `expect.poll(() => page.url())` with a 10s timeout is the right shape, but `page.waitForURL(/\/en\/auth\/login/)` is the idiomatic Playwright primitive for this exact case — it hooks into the navigation lifecycle instead of polling a getter. The task hint at line 97 of 11.md explicitly recommends `await page.waitForURL(/\/en\/auth\/login/)`. Functionally close, but `waitForURL` is more deterministic on CI (single navigation event vs poll interval).
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Swap line 14 for `await page.waitForURL(/\/en\/auth\/login$/)` then keep `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en\/auth\/login$/)` on the next line if you want a hard URL assertion. Aligns with task spec edge-case guidance and removes the poll loop.

non_blocking_findings.issue: AC9 says LangSwitcher click switches atomically cookie+URL+<html lang>+content. The spec checks URL, <html lang>, and content (button text), but not the i18n cookie. This is a legitimate gap if AC9 is read strictly; however the task description explicitly bounds the spec to ~30 LOC and lists only URL/lang/text/validation as mandatory checks, so it's a coverage trade-off rather than a defect. Also: the UK→EN validation message symmetry is asserted only on EN side; the Zod live-switch behaviour (re-running schema with new locale) is inferred, not directly contrasted. Flagging non-blocking because the task description and AC list both stop at the EN-side check.
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: If you want to tighten without bloat, add one line: `expect(await page.context().cookies()).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({ name: 'i18n_redirected', value: 'en' }))` after the URL assertion. Skip if you're holding the LOC line — current coverage matches what the task explicitly requires.

non_blocking_findings.issue: `test.use({ locale: 'uk-UA' })` at module scope pins the browser's Accept-Language for this file. This is correct for the test (default locale path `/auth/login` should resolve to uk via `prefix_except_default` strategy regardless of Accept-Language, since uk is the default), but it makes the assertion `toHaveAttribute('lang', 'uk')` partly tautological — even if locale-detection logic broke and fell back to Accept-Language, the test would still pass. Not a litmus failure (default-locale routing logic is what's being checked, and removing it would still break the URL regex), but worth noting that the lang assertion could be marginally weakened by this fixture.
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Optional: drop `test.use({ locale: 'uk-UA' })` and rely on URL-strategy-based default-locale resolution. If kept, document with a one-line comment why (e.g. `// pin Accept-Language to make root path deterministic across CI runners`).
